instructions: Put 6 cups water and the salt in a pot and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, peel the papaya, cut it in half and scoop out the seeds. Shred it on the large holes of a box grater into a big bowl. That should be about 7 cups. Use only what you need if there's extra.
Juice the limes, which should be about 1/4 cup. In a small bowl, stir together the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and the garlic, minced, until the sugar dissolves.
Add the shrimp to the boiling water and cook for 2 minutes, until pink and curled. Drain and rinse them under cold water. Cut each shrimp into 2 or 3 pieces.
Chop 1/3 cup each of the cilantro, mint and Thai basil. Roughly chop the peanuts.
Add the shrimp and the herbs to the papaya, pour the dressing over and toss until everything is coated.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more fish sauce.
Slice the Thai chili and put it in a small bowl on the table for the adults. Sprinkle the peanuts over the salad and serve it right away.
method_notes: No version read had a rating, so the lead is the best-read real version: Girl Cooks World's goi du du, with a lime, fish sauce, garlic, sugar and chile dressing over shredded green papaya, cooked shrimp, cilantro, mint, Thai basil and roasted peanuts. Food and the Fabulous agrees on the papaya, shrimp, herbs and fish sauce and lime dressing, but adds crisp dried shrimp and fried shallot, which are left out here for time. The lead's rau ram is replaced by more of the other herbs, as the lead itself suggests. Raw shrimp is poached in place of the lead's cooked shrimp, and the chile moves to the table so the salad stays mild. Check the fish sauce label for gluten.
